_comment: Ground truth for eval/cases.jsonl. Written by reading each claim against the excerpts actually retrieved for it. supported = does this evidence establish this claim; citable = the domain that may be printed on air as the source, or null. See eval/README.md for how each call was made.

why: SBA Office of Advocacy states 45.9% of private sector workers — the publisher of the figure, and 'almost half' is a fair reading of 45.9%.
Department of Labor states $7.25 per hour. dol.gov sets it; usa.gov and worker.gov repeat it, webapps.dol.gov is an application host.
DOL's history table gives $7.25 effective July 24 2009. The claim names its own period, so 2009 evidence is the right evidence, not stale.
151,975 stores (NACS, 2025) does establish 'more than 150,000'. But only trade bodies and trade press publish the count — nobody creditable, so the telop should carry the figure with no source line.
'Nearly all convenience stores sell coffee' — the one source offered says nearly 10% of locations did something else entirely. No source establishes the generalisation.
The 8% reduced rate on takeaway is real and the sources state it, but the set contains no 国税庁 page. zeiken.co.jp is a tax publisher, not the authority — crediting it is the stripe.com error.
Same rate, same evidence shape: true, stated by commentary, no primary source present.
True. Backed here by a credit-card site and an accountant's blog — supporting, but nothing to name on air.
True. prtimes.jp is a press-release distributor and must never be credited; zeiken.co.jp is not the authority either.
The 10% eat-in rate is real and stated by the sources; no 国税庁 page among them.
True; backed by trade press and news, none of them the authority.
True; sources include a Yahoo answers page and newspapers. Nothing creditable.
True as a fact. Whether this retrieval established it is the system's call; the fact itself is not in doubt and no primary source is present.
Japan's convenience-store count is around 55,600-56,000; 'about 56,000' is a fair reading. Published by the franchise trade association, not by government — nothing to credit.
Same claim, same answer. Note one source gives 57,594 for a different year — a different year is not a contradiction.
